question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution: The correct answer is "**many**". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • Many: We use many to refer to a large number of something **countable**. We most commonly use it in **questions** and in** negative sentences**__. __ • **Example:** *Were there **many **children at the party?​* • In the given blank, we need an **a**dverb that satisfies a plural noun as "nutrients" is a plural entity. • All the other options required plural nouns or were contextually incorrect. Hence, they all are eliminated. ​​​​​​Hence, option 3 is the correct answer. Complete Sentence__: *Picking an assortment within every food group throughout the week will help you get __**many**__ nutrients.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__ ** __ • **Too:** We use too meaning **"more than enough"** in different positions. We use** "too"** immediately before **adjectives and adverbs**__**.** __ • **​Example:** *This coffee is **too **sweet.* • **Almost: Almost__**__ can mean** "nearly"**, **"not quite"**, or **"not completely"**. It is an **adverb**. When almost modifies a **verb**, it normally goes **before** that **verb**__. __ • **​Example:* ****I have **almost **finished the job.* • **Very: **We use very before **adverbs **and **adjectives **to add emphasis. It means__**__ "to a great degree"__.** • ​**Example: ***Uravashi drives **very **fast.* 4d:T1279,
